leagues.name: Roshn Saudi League
notes: 18 clubs for 2026-27, from the Saudi Pro League official site. Season runs 13 Aug 2026 to 29 May 2027.
Title sponsor ROSHN Group (a PIF company); league partners include Saudia, Ma'aden, BSF, EA Sports, Sun Cola, Coffee Address, BCare and Baja (official site partner strip).

Several clubs are state- or PIF-owned: PIF owns Al-Nassr, Al-Ittihad and Al-Ahli and holds 30% of Al-Hilal (70% sold to Kingdom Holding, Sep 2026); Aramco owns Al-Qadsiah, NEOM owns NEOM SC, Diriyah Gate Development Authority runs Diriyah Club.

owners.name: NHC (National Housing Company)

owners.note: Set up by the ministry as its real-estate investment arm; state-owned.

owners.name: Saudia (Saudi Arabian Airlines)
owners.note: PIF holds the controlling stake in parent Saudi Arabian Airlines Corporation.

owners.name: Banque Saudi Fransi (BSF)
owners.note: Listed bank; PIF stake reported at ~16.19% (2026).

owners.name: stc (Saudi Telecom Company)
owners.note: PIF is the majority shareholder; parent of neoleap.

owners.name: Kingdom Holding Company (KHC)
owners.note: 78.1% held by Prince Alwaleed bin Talal; PIF holds 16.9%. Acquired 70% of Al-Hilal from PIF (Sep 2026).

unsourced: Kit sponsor PLACEMENTS (which brand sits on front vs back vs sleeve vs shorts) come from the Wikipedia 2026-27 season page 'Personnel and kits' table; the brief forbids citing Wikipedia, so treat placements as unconfirmed until checked against a club kit launch.

Al-Hilal front/main sponsor conflict: Wikipedia (in-season) lists NHC Innovation as main with Flynas front, Riyad Bank back, Tree Digital sleeve; 433FC (Jun 2026) says Savvy Games Group is the main front sponsor. Both PIF-linked; needs a club source.

Al-Nassr: HUMAIN confirmed as main 2026/27 sponsor (Campaign ME / Footy Headlines, 28-30 Jul 2026). A second front sponsor (Syndicate Holding Group, 'SHG', to 2028) and Gathern and AROYA Cruises are also reported; exact placements unconfirmed.
Al-Ittihad: 433FC (Jun 2026) says front sponsor ROSHN; Wikipedia lists no main sponsor and puts Flow Progressive Logistics front and TCL sleeve. Needs checking.
Al-Ettifaq kit maker conflict: Wikipedia says Jako, 433FC says Castore.
NEOM kit maker conflict: Wikipedia says Adidas, 433FC says Puma. Wikipedia also lists a 'SHG' front sponsor on Neom SC; whether it is the same SHG as Al-Nassr's is unconfirmed.
NEOM SC identity: the 2026-27 club is 'NEOM SC' (Neom), formerly Al-Suqoor; the Wikipedia and SPL lists differ in styling (Neom / Al-Diriyah vs Diriyah Club). ids chosen as 'neom' and 'diriyah'.
Aloula Aviation (Al-Qadsiah): the Wikipedia table links it to Aramco but ownership is not confirmed by a primary source; recorded with ownerId null.

NHC ownership: NHC says it was set up by and is supervised by the Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs and Housing (a state investment arm); some secondary sources call it 'state-owned'. Not confirmed as PIF-owned.
Banque Saudi Fransi PIF stake (~16.19%) is from a secondary aggregator (4pmarketingmix, Sep 2026); needs the BSF annual report.
ROSHN title deal term unknown; the original 2022 naming deal was widely reported as five years, so the current end date needs checking (Wikipedia lead).
PIF ownership of Al-Nassr, Al-Ittihad and Al-Ahli: 75% taken in 2023; AGBI (Aug 2026, fetch returned 403) reported PIF absorbing the remaining 25% held by non-profit foundations. Not re-verified.
Riyad Bank, Alinma Bank, flynas, Cenomi and Tree Digital have plausible state/PIF links (Riyad Bank, Alinma) but were recorded with ownerId null pending a primary source.

Kit makers (Nike, Adidas, Puma, Macron, Kappa, Jako, Castore, Offside, Laser, Hattrick, Black Panther, HH Sports) are recorded as sponsors here; the schema has no kit-maker placement, so they are not attached to kit entries.
Codes (ABH, AHL, ...) are conventional three-letter abbreviations, not from an official list.
